title: A G1 walk's verdict: .private/work/walks/<sha40>/verdict.json
description: Contract (PR f0) for the file the G1 real-set walk writes last (`scripts/walk/` and the `real-set-walk.js` workflow, PR f5) and `scripts/walk/ready.py` (PR f5), `scripts/factory/watch.py` (PR f3, the band's 'G1 main') and the walk-now hook (PR f6, through ready.py) read (docs/specs/factory.md 3.8 'real-set-walk.js', 5 'G1'). WRITE: after the script layer's `walk.json` exists, the agent layer has finished, every issue draft passed the leak scan and the triage is done, `scripts/walk/` writes `.private/work/walks/<sha40>/verdict.json` atomically; it is the last file written, so its existence means the walk is over. The folder name is the walked head's full sha. The file is private (under .private/) but holds no free text anyway: only enums, numbers and ids, so `scripts/walk/sanitize.py` can publish from it by allowlist (finish-line item code, defect class, screen, numeric delta). READ: `ready.py <ref>` passes only when the two most recent verdicts of main (by `finished_at`) both have `result` PASS with no FAIL between them and the newer one is on `<ref>`'s current head, or on an earlier head whose diff to it touches no product path (`vextrus/`, `engine/`, `web/src/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`); ready.py takes the head from `sha` and the diff from git. THE PASS RULE (stated once, here and in docs/specs/factory.md 5 'G1'): `result` is PASS if and only if (1) every element of `checks` has status PASS (UNSET, a check with no expectation, fails); (2) every element of `agent_layer.items` has status PASS (NOT_WALKED fails, as does FAIL) and all twelve walked items, M0-FL1 to M0-FL11 and M0-FL13, are listed once each; (3) `agent_layer.blocks` is 0; and (4) `agent_layer.misleading` is 0. Otherwise `result` is FAIL; there is no third result. The schema enforces the PASS direction (the top-level if/then); `scripts/walk/` computes `result` by this rule and `scripts/walk/tests/` tests both directions. THE ITEM CODES: M0-FLn is item n of docs/specs/M0.md 'Finish line', 'The owner's walk' (n = 1 to 13; the mapping table is in docs/specs/factory.md 5). The prefix keeps them apart from the finish codes FL1 and FL2 of docs/research/qs-defaults.md and docs/specs/M2.md.

sha.description: The walked head, the folder's name.

ref.description: What was walked: `main` for a gate walk. ready.py counts only verdicts with ref `main` toward 'the two most recent on main'.

checks.description: The script layer's three measured checks (`web/e2e/real/walk.spec.ts`), once per Development Set walked. Selectors use roles and test ids, never a title.

burden.description: G5, the QS's burden, counted beside check 3: one element per (set, Discipline), from the screen and the API on a real read. Counts only.

agent_layer.description: `/real-set-walk`: `ux-critic` (by eye) and `qs-critic` (burden) walk the finish-line items M0-FL1 to M0-FL11 and M0-FL13 (docs/specs/factory.md 5's table; M0-FL12, the owner's real-drawing check on main, is dropped from G1 because each merged engine head's posting run covers it). Invariant (tested): len(findings) = issues_drafted + dedup_comments, and blocks and misleading are the counts of findings with severity BLOCKS and with misleading true.

items.description: The verdict per finish-line item walked. A PASS verdict lists all twelve walked items once each (the top-level if/then).

item.description: M0-FL1 to M0-FL11 and M0-FL13: item n of docs/specs/M0.md 'Finish line' (docs/specs/factory.md 5's table).

status.description: The item's status, one of three: PASS: walked, and the item holds as docs/specs/M0.md words it (findings of severity OTHER may stand under it); FAIL: walked, and the item does not hold as worded (a finding under it says why); NOT_WALKED: not walked (no time, a crash, a screen that would not open). Only PASS lets the walk's `result` be PASS: FAIL and NOT_WALKED both fail it.

leak_scan.description: The leak scan (`python -m tools.leakscan dir .private/work/walks/<sha40>/` plus every issue draft) ran before this file was written. A walk with hits is not written as a verdict; the field exists so a consumer can refuse a file whose scan was not clean.

check.description: reads_complete: (1) every file's read completes. act_p95_during_read: (2) act p95 (confirm, answer, exclude, undo) while a later file is still reading (where D1 lived). questions_per_discipline: (3) Questions per Discipline by kind (D2), with the burden counts.

set.description: The Development Set's slug, the name of its expectation file `.private/work/walk-expect/<set>.json`.

status.description: PASS: measured within `expected`. FAIL: measured outside it, or not measured. UNSET: no expectation exists for this check (`expected` is null). FAIL and UNSET both fail the walk's `result`.

measured.description: The numbers the walk measured; keys by check. reads_complete: {files, completed}. act_p95_during_read: {p95_ms, samples}. questions_per_discipline: {questions_max_per_discipline, disciplines}.

oneOf.description: The limits, from Q5 and the Answer Key's counts, same keys as `measured` where they compare (reads_complete: {files}; act_p95_during_read: {p95_ms_max}; questions_per_discipline: {questions_max_per_discipline}). Never taken from a walk's own recording.

expected.description: null exactly when status is UNSET.

discipline.description: A Market Discipline's name (a Library row, CONTEXT.md), never drawing text.

questions_by_kind.description: Open Questions by the product's Question kind code (for example `low_confidence`), each a count.

questions_total.description: The sum of questions_by_kind. Q5's limit: 3 or fewer per Discipline.

bulk_confirmable_sheets.description: Sheets the QS can confirm in bulk. Q5's limit: 80 % or more of `sheets`.

false_continuation_questions.description: Continuation Questions the Answer Key says were not continuations; null when no expectation exists. Q5's limit: 0.

finding.description: One finding. No free-text field exists: the evidence stays in .private/work/walks/<sha40>/ under `id`. Exactly one of `issue` and `dedup_comment_on` is non-null (the finding became an issue draft, or a comment on an open `walk` issue).

id.description: The finding id naming its evidence folder.

item.description: The finish-line item it was found under (M0-FL1 to M0-FL11 and M0-FL13).

defect_class.description: A class code from `scripts/walk/sanitize.py`'s allowlist (for example `act_waits_on_read`).

screen.description: A screen code from the same allowlist (the route's name, never a title).

delta.description: The numeric delta against the expectation, or null when the finding has none.

severity.description: BLOCKS fails the walk. Every other finding of any severity still becomes an issue or a dedup comment.

misleading.description: True when the product shows something that misleads the QS; fails the walk.

issue.description: The issue number drafted for it, or null if it became a dedup comment.

dedup_comment_on.description: The open `walk` issue it commented on (exact (defect_class, screen) match, or `jev same-issue` at 0.8 or more), or null if it became an issue.
